title: Table S5. External material and energy benchmarks.
rows: CO2 feed, 1.4 t/t methanol
IRENA: approximately 1.38. Rosental 1.441. Sollai 1.447 [S4,S5,S6].
Comparable feed requirements across different purge, by-product and yield assumptions. The exact coefficient is the DEA reference [11].
Hydrogen feed, 0.1917 t/t methanol
IRENA: approximately 0.19. Rosental 0.203. Sollai 0.208 [S4,S5,S6].
The adopted process has relatively high hydrogen utilisation within these designs.
ARA methanol yield, 0.7129 t/t raw source CO2
Approximate stoichiometric ceiling: 32/44 = 0.7273 t/t. Independent process yields follow their reported feed requirements [S4,S5,S6].
The yield satisfies material conservation. Its exact value retains the 0.998 conditioning-recovery assumption.
Electrolysis and BoP, 54.5 kWh/kgH2
Low-temperature system electricity approximately 50–55 kWh/kgH2 [S7]. Sollai reports 55.8 for the initial proton exchange membrane (PEM) system [S6].
System electricity is supported at this scale. Delivery pressure and compression coverage require their own interface definition.
ARA electrolysis electricity, 7.448 MWh/t raw source CO2
Published hydrogen requirements and system electricity provide the component comparison [S4, S6, S7].
Derived from 0.1367 tH2 per raw source tonne. It equals 10.45 MWh per tonne of methanol.
Conversion module, 11.14 MWh/t methanol
IRENA 10–11 with supplied CO2. Rosental current electrolysis plus synthesis entries give 10.34 [S4, S5].
Source handling is outside this module. Electric steam, auxiliaries and heat recovery explain differences among configurations.
Full ARA methanol route, 8.811 MWh/t raw source CO2 or 12.36 MWh/t methanol
Sollai Table 7 gives 12.33 MWh/t methanol from reported annual electricity and production [S6].
Similar electricity scale with different capture-heat provision. The comparison retains that distinction.
Electrolysis share, 84.53% of ARA route electricity
Independent process studies identify electrolysis as the dominant electricity consumer [S4,S6].
The percentage is calculated for the present route. Electricity, expense and emissions shares have different denominators.
Capture regeneration heat, ARA 2.592 and UK 2.700 GJth/tCO2
Advanced-solvent references near 2.2–2.9. Conventional 30 wt% MEA near 3.6–4.0 [18,S8].
Advanced-capture engineering analogues. The values retain the chosen solvent and utility assumptions.
Full ARA storage route, 0.8609 MWh/t raw source CO2
Literature heat duties converted with the specified boiler efficiency, plus separate compression evidence [18,S9,S8,S10].
The complete-route balance includes capture. The remaining route modules consume 0.09854 MWh/t after capture is excluded.
Compression and drying, ARA 0.08465 and US 0.1097 MWh/tCO2
Post-combustion compression 292–425 kJ/kgCO2, equivalent to 0.0811–0.1181 MWh/t [S9].
A numerical engineering comparator with different inlet, cooling and drying conditions.
UK and US storage routes, 0.9546 and 0.1236 MWh/t
Capture-heat and compression studies support the component burdens [18,S9,S10].
UK includes additional separation and electric heat. The US decision inlet follows existing process separation.
Yulin high- and low-pressure storage routes, 0.02187 and 0.1962 MWh/t
Published native stream conditions and injection design [24]. Compression theory supplies the pressure response [S9].
High native pressure reduces additional compression. The exact route totals are model calculations under the retained interfaces.
ARA methanol-to-storage electricity ratio, 10.23
Literature establishes the additional electrolytic-hydrogen requirement and the distinct storage compression burden [S4,S9].
A ratio specific to the adopted source and heat supply.
Product, by-product and conditioning carbon, 0.9802, 0.01782 and 0.002 t corresponding CO2 mass/t source
DEA by-product allowance [11] and the 1.375 tCO2/t methanol oxidation factor in official fuel accounting.
The carbon balance closes to one raw source tonne. Product purity and conditioning recovery are different quantities.
Full-market substitution, 140 MtCO2 feed/y, 19.17 MtH2/y and 1045 TWh/y
Approximately 100 Mt/y methanol market reference [10] and process coefficients [11,S4].
Conditional scale multiplication. The electricity quantity covers electrolysis and BoP. It represents resource demand rather than net mitigation.
precision: Transcribed displayed values. Full-precision computational data are separate.
